transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because I just... I feel like I can't really settle in my own body anymore. It's mostly when I'm supposed to just sit quietly and... deal with paperwork, or go over shared household plans. I just... yeah. That's mainly it.
When this happens, does it come on suddenly and intensely, like a wave that peaks and then fades, or is it more of a constant, low-level feeling that stays with you most of the day?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't exactly paid attention to how it starts. It just... happens when I have to sit down and do those things. I don't really know if it's a wave or... something else.
Does this feeling of being unable to settle only happen during tasks like paperwork or planning, or do you notice similar restlessness and unease in other situations throughout your day as well?

I guess... it's not just when I'm doing paperwork. Um, even on days when I'm just home... I don't really sit still. I'll start the laundry, and then I'll look at my emails, and then I'm fixing a drawer or looking at the calendar. I just... keep moving. It feels sort of like... I'm being pushed from the inside, I guess. I don't really take breaks.

When you notice yourself unable to settle, are you also experiencing a lot of worried thoughts running through your mind about things like your responsibilities or what might go wrong, or is it more just a physical urge to keep moving without a lot of worrying thoughts attached?

Um... I don't know if I'm really worrying. I mean, everyone worries a little, right? But... mostly it's just that I feel like I need to get up and do something. I don't really think about it too much.
Thinking back, did you notice this kind of restlessness or trouble sitting still even as a child or teenager, or is this something that's really only started more recently in your adult life?

Um... I guess it's always been like this. Even back in elementary school. I don't really like thinking about it, but... I was always the kid with the really messy desk. I'd forget permission slips and stuff like that. And... my teachers would send notes home saying I talked out of turn, or... that I just wouldn't stay in my seat. So... yeah. It's not a new thing.

latest_inference.note: Childhood-onset hyperactivity, inattentiveness (messy desk, forgotten permission slips, talking out of turn, inability to stay seated) strongly supports a neurodevelopmental pattern rather than anxiety. Patient denies prominent worry thoughts, reducing likelihood of GAD or unspecified anxiety disorder, so F41.9 and F41.1 are ruled out.
